Vamos Taxi — content & photography checklist Internal — not for customer distribution

Content & photography still needed

Every page below is built and working. This is what's still missing before it can leave placeholder state — decisions first, since each one settles more than one page at once, then photography, then each page's own copy and numbers. Nothing here should be guessed: every fare stays CHF 000 and every pending fact stays a labelled placeholder until it's answered.

Settle once — unlocks several pages

Decisions first

  1. Carrier or booking intermediary? Whether Vamos is legally the carrier or an intermediary changes the liability and subcontracting clauses, and whether About can keep saying “our drivers.” → Terms, About
  2. Vehicle lineup — final classes, names and capacities. Economy (3 passengers / 3 bags) and a Van class were confirmed in July, but Van's own capacity is on file as both 7/8 and 8/8, and the live code now also ships a “Business” and a “First” class whose capacities were never given at all. One settled table — class, passenger capacity, bag capacity, which of them actually launch — before more code or copy points at any of it. → Home, Checkout, Confirmation, About, FAQ, Cancellation
  3. The three cancellation shares. One source promises a full refund inside 24 hours; another grants 75% and keeps 25%. Both are live promises on file at once. → Cancellation, Terms, FAQ
  4. One company address. Older material gives a Zürich address; current pages give Bleicherstrasse 16, Dietikon. → Privacy, Imprint, Terms
  5. One support email. Three addresses are on file, including a personal address in an old terms draft. → Contact, Privacy, Terms, footer
  6. One payment-method list. Terms names Amex/Visa/Mastercard/cash/bank transfer; FAQ names Visa/Mastercard/Apple Pay/TWINT/PayPal. → Terms, footer, checkout
  7. Which analytics tool. Vercel Analytics, PostHog or Google Analytics — changes the cookie table and the privacy clause. → Privacy, Cookies
  8. Is crash reporting (Sentry) “strictly necessary,” or consent-gated? As written today it sits under Analytics, so declining analytics also turns off crash reporting. → Cookies, Privacy
  9. Does live chat exist in V1? The old site advertised 24/7 chat; three FAQ answers and the footer currently assume it still does. → FAQ, Contact, footer
  10. Build “Become a partner,” or unlink it? A draft exists (copy and fields only, no photography) but it sits outside the agreed scope. If it's cut, delete the file and drop the footer and About links to it. → Footer, About, Become a partner
  11. Is automated flight-status tracking in scope for V1? Other docs say postpone it; the home page field already does live polling against a flight-data API key that isn't confirmed. → Home
  12. Is “book by the hour” launching? The tab and fields exist; scope says “if approved for launch,” not yet decided. → Home, footer
  13. Court of venue for disputes — the old clause names a third party's registered office. → Terms
  14. Which channels can cancel a booking? Terms says account only; FAQ says chat, WhatsApp or email. → Cancellation, FAQ
  15. Is consent logged server-side? Changes the consent-log retention period and the engineering behind the cookie banner. → Cookies, Privacy

The brand owns exactly one usable vehicle photo today

Photography

Same brief wherever these land: premium black vehicles, cool daylight, no warm filter, no grain, no people-first lifestyle shots.

  • Home & About hero. Both currently show the same placeholder: a black car at night, warm amber cabin light, wet asphalt — the opposite of the cool-daylight rule. About also captions it “Arrivals hall at Zurich airport,” though the shot is a car door and interior, not an airport hall. Needs a real cool-daylight arrivals or curbside shot, captioned to match.
  • Economy vehicle. No photo exists — falls back to an icon tile on Home's fleet cards and About's fleet section.
  • Business vehicle. Same — no photo, and its capacity was never confirmed either (Decision 2).
  • “First” class, if it is launching at all (Decision 2): no photo, no brief.
  • Founder portrait. Ben Othman Houssein, cool daylight, no studio background, for About's “Founder-led, and answerable” section. A founder-led story with a stock face is worse than one with none, so this stays empty until the real portrait exists.
  • Driver at the curb, with a name board — Home's “why Vamos” section.
  • Vehicle on an alpine / ski-corridor route — same section.
  • Chauffeur at the rear door — same section.
  • Destination / lifestyle photography. No library beyond the single Van street photo; needed for any future route or coverage imagery.
  • Sign-in / reset-password side panel. Charcoal and the checker mark only today; the one Van photo is wired up behind a toggle if it should be used there instead.
  • Payment marks. Visa, Mastercard, TWINT, Apple Pay, PayPal, cash — plain text chips in the footer today; swap for the real marks once the provider list is confirmed (Decision 6).
  • Social platform marks. Instagram, Facebook and LinkedIn icons must come from each platform's own brand kit (the icon library dropped its brand glyphs); the footer currently uses plain glyphs.

Everything else, by page

Copy & numbers

Home

  • The CHF fare matrix — fixed routes and surcharges. The last real money gap; every fare on the page is a placeholder until it lands.
  • The vehicle-lineup decision (2) — drives the fleet cards directly.
  • Hero photography (see above).

About

  • Coverage list — every city, resort and cross-border destination served, and which are seasonal. One answer fills About's routes section and the booking widget's destination list.
  • Support languages, and which languages drivers speak.
  • How many hours before pickup you get the driver's name, plate and number (shown twice on this page).
  • Founder portrait, Economy and Business photography (see Photography above).

Contact

  • Support email (Decision 5), response-time commitment, support hours, and chat hours if chat ships (Decision 9).
  • Facebook, Instagram, YouTube and Trustpilot profile URLs — a domain exists but nothing is linked yet.

FAQ

  • Which airports offer meet-and-greet.
  • Shares its remaining answers with Decisions 2, 3, 9 and 12, and the driver-lead-time / support-language facts from About.

Manage a booking, account, bookings, booking detail

  • All read off the same refund-share numbers as Cancellation (Decision 3) — nothing new to supply once that's settled.
  • Verification-code expiry time and how many resend attempts are allowed (phone verification, reached from Account).
  • Guest manage-booking link: does the access token expire only after the trip, or after a fixed duration regardless of pickup date?

Sign in, reset password

  • Whether the side panel keeps the one Van photo or stays photo-free (see Photography above).

Become a partner — draft only, pending Decision 10

  • Reply-time commitment.
  • Which vehicle classes / body types partners can apply with.
  • Which licences and permits are actually required.
  • Whether phone, email, or both, are mandatory.

Terms & conditions

  • Registered legal name (the register shows “Vamos Taxi,” no GmbH — confirm which is correct).
  • Extra-stop fee; city-stay minutes and fee (only a €15 figure is on file, needs a CHF number); oversized-item fee; case dimensions and hand-luggage allowance.
  • Airport and standard waiting minutes included, extra-waiting rate, no-show call attempts (shared with Cancellation), complaint response window in days.
  • Legal text to draft: contracting party, subcontracting, refusal of carriage & soiling, refused/unaccompanied items, dispute-resolution body, liability, force majeure, court of venue (Decision 11).
  • Plus Decisions 1, 3, 4, 5, 6 above.

Cancellation & refunds

  • Free-cancellation window (hours); large-vehicle seat threshold and its own booking window; modification deadline; driver-no-show refund share; refund decision days and payout days; voucher validity period.
  • Legal text: consequential costs when no driver arrives, disruption outcome, voucher terms.
  • Plus Decisions 3 and 12 above.

Privacy policy

  • Data-protection-officer name, or confirmation none is required; EU representative.
  • Data-hosting regions for Supabase, Vercel, Resend, Sentry and the analytics tool.
  • Retention periods: booking records (years), finance, logs, consent log; data-subject-request response time in days.
  • Legal text: statutory basis per data use, transfer mechanism per destination — the old Privacy Shield clause cannot be reused.
  • Plus Decisions 4, 7, 8 and 15 above.

Cookie policy & banner

  • Real cookie names and exact durations for: session, consent, hosting, language, recent-address, analytics, error-monitoring, marketing.
  • How many months a consent choice is stored.
  • Plus Decisions 7, 8 and 15 above.

Imprint

  • UID / company registration number — not published anywhere yet.
  • Supervisory authority and licence; dispute-resolution body; liability disclaimer text.
  • Photography, brand-agency and build-agency credits — only if each party agrees to be named.

Site-wide

  • Qurova's webfont / redistribution licence — only Poppins has a licence file on record; confirm the foundry grants web rights before this ships.
